items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: The name 'Lally' appears only in the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn ('...where Lally's got a nice house and shit...'). The [INTERVIEWEE] does not mention Lally, nor does the interviewee respond to or acknowledge the name in the provided transcript.

ctx.x: She used to confess the same sin over and over. same sin over and over. And the priest asked her one day, gee, now let's get together here now. How many times has this happened to you? She told her she was raped. And she said, now, how often has this happened to you? She says, oh, it happened a long time ago, but I'd just love to talk about it. It's fucked, see?

That's what I'm getting outside, man. I'll show you. I'll show you. Look over there. And my main scribe was trying to get in the town and stay there while trying to give me a place where Lally's got a nice house and shit. I don't care if she had a husband. I don't even care. Even that landlady, you get a free rent to clothes wash. She's a fool. I got to throw her in many places, too, man. Well, we go from here now.

When you were first started, were you studying music? Or who did you start thinking? No, I started out thinking first, then I started to study. Later? Oh, yeah. After I was playing professionally about two years, then I started to study. Because you couldn't play in bands. You couldn't go to a pit or anything with that if you couldn't read. Well, from Ray Miller, yeah, I went to Ted Lewis. That was a nice sentence. Eight years hardly. How many years? Eight years. Eight years. I don't know what a depression was. I…
